answer: Ration identities with blind-signed passes. Each epoch an issuer checks one scarce credential per operator, such as a verified payment card, and blindly signs a single token; the agent unblinds it and spends it to register or vote. The blinding cipher means the issuer can't link the token to the card, yet the card can't be reused for a second pass that epoch. A tide of fake keys then needs a tide of real cards, while an honest newcomer gets in with the ease of a zephyr.
